title: CurseForge in Hosting, and pick your source in Discover

entries.text: Server Mods and Plugins tabs have a Modrinth / CurseForge switch: search and install CurseForge mods (Fabric, Quilt, Forge, NeoForge) and Bukkit plugins (Paper, Purpur), with their required dependencies.
New server → Modpack: pick a modpack from Modrinth or CurseForge. CurseForge modpacks install the mods the server needs, leave out game-only ones, and copy the pack’s configs.
Mods that only work in the game (like Sodium) are checked after download and refused with a clear reason, whichever site they come from.
Choose where to search: Both, Modrinth or CurseForge. Astra remembers your choice.

title: CurseForge works out of the box

entries.text: CurseForge is now built into Astra: search, browse and install CurseForge mods and modpacks, and import CurseForge modpack .zip files, with nothing to set up. Settings → Integrations simply shows CurseForge as Connected.

title: CurseForge, done properly

entries.text: Import a CurseForge modpack .zip (Library → Import, or drag it onto Astra): Astra shows what’s inside — Minecraft version, mod loader, how many mods, configs — before installing. Reading the .zip needs no CurseForge key.

Installing downloads every mod CurseForge allows, checks each one, copies the pack’s configs and settings, and shows progress with a Cancel button. If something fails, nothing half-installed is left behind.

Some mod authors only allow downloads from the CurseForge website. Astra lists those files with a Download button for each, then finds them in your Downloads folder, checks they’re the right files and adds them. You can finish this later from the instance page.

Settings → Integrations → CurseForge: connect once with your API key, test the connection, replace or remove the key. The key is encrypted on this PC (Windows key store), never shown to the app’s pages, never put in backups or logs.

No more “CurseForge needs a key” screen: connect right inside Browse or the import window. Clear messages for a rejected key, rate limits, CurseForge being down, deleted projects and files, and no internet.
CurseForge files whose authors block app downloads are no longer fetched around that choice.
Opening Settings with an old link no longer shows an error.

title: Endless scrolling, and server settings without restarting

entries.text: Discover stopped after the first 24 results. Now it keeps loading as you scroll — mods, modpacks, shaders, everything — until there’s nothing left.
Browse loads the next page by itself when you scroll down (no more clicking “Load more”).

Change settings while the server runs: difficulty, game mode, PvP, monsters, the Nether, the whitelist and the idle kick switch on straight away — no restart. If something does need a restart (like max players), Astra says which and gives you a “Restart now” button.
On Minecraft 26.x the PvP, Monsters and Nether switches were missing from Settings (Minecraft made them game rules). They’re back, and they work.
Switch between playit.gg and “Home only” while the server runs — the tunnel opens or closes right away.

title: Astra grows up: mod health, server tools, backups and more

entries.text: Mod health: the new Health button on a modded instance checks every mod for missing dependencies, wrong Minecraft or loader versions, duplicates and mods that can’t run together — with a score, what to do first, and one-click fixes you confirm.
Check for updates and compare two instances side by side from the same page.
Server details (ⓘ on your saved servers): how often it was online over the last week, which software it runs, your join history, notes, and an instance to always join with.
Alerts for a single server when it goes online or offline.
Connection test: when you can’t join, Astra checks each step (address, DNS, port, Minecraft, version) and tells you which one fails and why.
Notifications: a bell in the title bar keeps everything Astra tells you — friends, servers, modpack updates, backups, new Minecraft versions. Choose what pops up.
Backups & Sync: back up your settings, servers and every instance’s setup, restore just what you pick, and sync between PCs through a OneDrive / Dropbox / Google Drive folder.
Discover: one search over Modrinth and CurseForge for mods, modpacks, resource packs, shaders, maps and community content.
Analytics: your play time per day, per instance and per version, session history and crash trends.
Assistant: explains crashes, launcher errors and server problems, points at the mods involved and suggests fixes — nothing changes until you confirm, and every fix can be undone.
Developer Hub (in Connect): add third-party integrations with permissions you control.
Play time was counted twice for a game still running when you closed Astra while your hosted servers were stopping.
Passwords, tokens and webhooks in mod config files are never put in backups.

title: Solaris is now Astra 🌙

entries.text: New name: Solaris is now Astra. Your instances, worlds, servers, settings and sign-ins all stay — nothing to set up again.

New moon look: the Astra theme (deep night blue with a moon-blue accent), the Moonlight background with stars, and a new moon icon. Your look switches to it once; pick another one any time in Settings → Appearance.
Invite links now start with astra:// — old solaris:// links still work.

Waypoints: save places, or take them straight from save files — where a player is, their last death, their bed and the world spawn. Share them as a code (or plain coordinates) that friends paste into Astra. On a server you host: teleport a player to a waypoint or post it in chat.
A Waypoints button on every player in Stats.
Astra opens about a third faster: the window appears before the rest of Astra has loaded, and the start screen fades away quicker.

title: Solaris Connect, faster launches and a much bigger Hosting

entries.text: New Connect page: every service Solaris connects to — maps, friends, servers and player tools — with its real status (connected, ready, needs setup, problem), settings, compatibility with your servers, recent problems and documentation. Nothing pretends to work: things not built yet say “Planned”, things that would need an online Solaris service say “Unavailable”.
Server monitoring: checks your favourite (or all saved) servers every few minutes and tells you when one comes online, goes offline, or a friend joins it.
Desktop alerts for the servers you host: online, crashed, stopped, a player joined or left — while Solaris is in the background.

Web maps: BlueMap (3D), Pl3xMap (2D) or Dynmap on a hosted server’s new Map tab — Solaris installs and sets it up, and the map opens inside Solaris with live player positions. Map links: open the web map of any server you play on.
Stats: play time, deaths, distance, mining, mobs and advancements (with dates, “X of Y”) for every player of your worlds and hosted servers, read from the save files.
Inventory viewer: inventory, armour, off hand and ender chest (with shulker box and bundle contents, real item pictures) for servers you host and your own worlds. Read-only.
New server in 4 steps — Server Type, World, Performance, Review — with cards for Paper, Purpur, Vanilla, Modpack, Fabric, Quilt, NeoForge, Forge and Bedrock, and a RAM hint for the optimal range.
Quilt servers, and Mojang’s own Bedrock Dedicated Server (phones, consoles and Windows join directly).
Performance tab with CPU, RAM, uptime and a 30-minute graph.
Scheduler: your own timed commands, messages, restarts and backups (every X minutes, daily at a time, or when the server starts), plus automatic restarts.
Tunnels tab: every playit.gg tunnel with its address, local port and which server uses it — turn on/off or delete.
Players: everyone who ever joined, with search, filters (online, operators, whitelisted, banned), last seen and play time.
Mods tab: Server mods and Client mods (what players need, plus extra game-only mods for the play instance).

Settings: gameplay, performance and security switches, your own Java and JVM arguments, optimized flags, restart after a crash, resource pack (upload a .zip or paste a link), Copy server, and Export / Import a server to move it to another PC.
Backups: countdown to the next automatic backup, and auto-backup settings right there. Worlds: import a world folder, .zip or .mcworld.
Deleting a server also deletes its playit.gg tunnels.
Add friends with an offline (cracked) account.
Friends on your running servers show as online live, not only for 5 minutes.

Join codes say whether the server needs a Microsoft account; an offline account gets a clear warning before joining. When an offline account is turned away from your server, Solaris offers to allow offline accounts (with the whitelist).
Switching “Require Microsoft accounts” keeps everyone’s inventory and progress — Solaris moves their save to the right ID on the next start.

Faster Play: Solaris module updates are checked at most every 6 hours (and all at once), the sounds-and-textures check runs while the game loads, and signing in happens at the same time as the file checks.

title: Voice chat tunnels that work on free playit.gg

entries.text: Voice chat uses playit.gg’s free “MC: Simple Voice Chat” tunnel, asked for the same way the playit.gg website does — before, playit.gg refused it (TunnelTypeRequiresDescription) and voice chat showed as disconnected.
Bedrock players get playit.gg’s free “Minecraft Bedrock (NetherNet)” tunnel the same way.
Voice chat address box in a server’s Settings: paste the address of a tunnel you made on playit.gg yourself. A voice_host you set is never erased any more.
If playit.gg still says no, Solaris shows the exact free tunnel to add on playit.gg, an Open playit.gg button and “I made it — check again”.

title: Hosting in its own window

entries.text: Pop out: open Hosting in its own window from the Hosting page or any server. Clicking it again brings that window forward on the server you clicked.
Both windows stay live — console, players, tunnels and crash help update in each. The Solaris button brings the main window back, and the Hosting window remembers its size and place.
Closing the main window while the Hosting window is open keeps Solaris running, so you can host from the small window alone.

title: Voice chat and Bedrock tunnels fixed

entries.text: Voice chat and Bedrock tunnels are made on playit.gg again (playit.gg answered “validation” before). Solaris now tries playit.gg’s current request first, then the same kind of request that makes your Minecraft tunnel, so it works on every account.
Bedrock tunnels use playit.gg’s NetherNet type — the connection the newest Bedrock Edition uses.
When playit.gg turns a tunnel down, Solaris shows its full reason instead of a single word.
If playit.gg can’t be reached when you press Connect, Solaris no longer gets stuck on “waiting for approval”.

title: Bedrock players, crash helper, voice chat and setup codes

entries.text: Simple Voice Chat in one click: Solaris installs the mod or plugin, makes a UDP tunnel on playit.gg and sets voice_host for you. Turn it on when creating a server or in its Settings.
Setup codes: copy a server’s whole setup (software, version, game settings, mods/plugins, voice chat, schedules) as one code and paste it into New server to make the same server again.
Join codes: send friends a short JOIN- code; they paste it in Hosting → Join with code.
Connect playit.gg with a setup code (the secret key from playit.gg) instead of approving in the browser.

New server now lets you set game mode, difficulty, world type, seed, view distance, MOTD, PvP, hardcore, whitelist, offline accounts, the playit.gg tunnel name, and starter extras like EssentialsX, LuckPerms, Chunky, WorldEdit, spark and ViaVersion.
Automation: automatic backups (keeps the newest ones), scheduled restarts with a 1-minute warning, and start servers with Windows.
Players: change game mode, teleport, heal, message, make or remove operators, ban and unban from the Players tab.
Bedrock players: phone, Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and Windows players can join your Java server. Solaris installs Geyser + Floodgate, sets them up and makes the playit.gg tunnel.

Crash helper: when a server stops by itself, Solaris explains why in plain words (missing mod, mod for another version, game-only mod, out of memory, port in use…) with a one-click fix. Also under “Why did it stop?”.
Pre-generate the world with Chunky from the Worlds tab, with a progress bar — less lag when players explore.
Lag check: TPS, tick time and CPU in plain words, plus a spark report that shows what causes lag.
Discord alerts: post to a channel when the server goes online, stops, crashes, or players join and leave.
Game instance for a server: one click makes an instance with the server’s version, loader and mods (plus voice chat); Join uses it straight away.
Friends: your running servers show with who’s on them and a join-code button; friends who join your server show as online; the Join box takes JOIN- codes.
Copy from an instance: pick one of your instances and copy its mods into your server in one click. Mods that only work in the game (Sodium, minimaps, zoom and so on) are left out for you.
Add files from PC: pick .jar mods or plugins from your computer, or drag them onto the Mods/Plugins tab.

Solaris checks every mod before adding it: wrong mod loader, client-only mods and the Solaris client mod are skipped with a reason, and mods made for another Minecraft version are flagged, because they usually stop the server from starting.
Adding a newer copy of a mod or plugin replaces the old one instead of keeping both.

title: Hosting fixes: player count, whitelist, duplicate mods

entries.text: The player count stayed at 0 when people joined servers on Minecraft 26.x. Joins and leaves are now counted correctly (also for players who time out).

Whitelisting players on servers that allow offline accounts didn’t work — they were still refused. Solaris now uses the right player ID for the server’s mode, and the running server picks it up right away.
Switching “Require Microsoft accounts” on or off keeps your whitelist and operators working.
Servers created with a modpack could get Fabric API and Lithium twice. The modpack’s own copies are used now, and duplicates already there are turned off automatically when the server starts.
Join from the server page only lists instances with the same Minecraft version, and says when you need to make one.

title: Playit.gg hosting made automatic

entries.text: Pick Playit.gg when you create a server and Solaris does the rest: installs and starts the playit.gg agent, creates the Minecraft tunnel for that server and shows its real public address — no tunnel setup on playit.gg.
Live progress while the server is created: preparing, downloading, installing playit.gg, starting the agent, creating the tunnel, waiting for the address, server ready.
The first time only, playit.gg asks you to approve Solaris once in your browser (sign in or continue as a guest). After that every new server gets its address automatically.
Server page: tunnel status light, Copy, How to join (instructions you can send to friends), Invite link, Restart tunnel and Stop/Start tunnel.
Each server keeps its own tunnel and the same address every time — saved between restarts, never duplicated.
The light only turns green once playit.gg is really connected and the server is up.
If playit.gg stops accepting this PC, Solaris says so and asks you to connect again instead of retrying forever in the background.
A port already used by another program is detected before the server is created, and “auto” picks a free one.
The playit.gg agent is checked against its official checksum, and always closes with Solaris.

title: Browse fixes: modpack pages open properly

entries.text: Clicking a modpack (or any project with lots of screenshots) opened its page off to the side or completely off the screen. Every project page now opens in the middle.
Project descriptions no longer show raw web code instead of links: links, badges, images, centred text, lists, code and spoilers now look like they do on Modrinth.
All other dialogs in Solaris are kept on screen too, however wide their content is.
Choosing a modpack for a new server now picks its latest stable version instead of a beta.

title: A bigger Solaris Client, better Discord, hosting and skin fixes

entries.text: 8 new HUD pieces: armor with durability, potion effects with time left, speed, reach, combo counter, day counter, memory and server address. Drag them anywhere in “Edit HUD layout”.
New in the Right Shift menu: toggle sneak, no hurt camera shake, no view bobbing and max brightness — turning one off gives you your own setting back.
Pick the accent and HUD text colour, turn the text shadow on or off, and copy your coordinates in one click.
The menu is now split into HUD, Features and Style, and fits smaller windows.
Your Discord status follows what you do: the page you’re on in Solaris, the main menu, your singleplayer world, the server you joined, or hosting a world for friends.
Hosting a server shows it on Discord with the player count (like “2 of 10”) and the address to join.
Privacy settings and streamer mode apply instantly, and Solaris never sends Discord more updates than it allows.
You can now wear Minecraft’s default skins (Steve, Alex and the others) — the Wear button used to stay greyed out.
A skin Mojang accepted no longer shows an error when Mojang is slow to update your profile.
The Skins page follows you when you switch accounts, and says when you’re already wearing the selected skin.
A server left running after Solaris closed or updated no longer blocks the next start with “Address already in use” — Solaris closes the old copy first, or tells you what is using the port.
New servers add you to the whitelist and as an operator, so you can’t be locked out of your own server.
When someone is turned away by the whitelist, Solaris tells you and offers “Add to whitelist”.
The Players tab updates when someone joins or leaves, renamed servers update right away, and crash messages say which server stopped.

title: Solaris on Linux, faster and steadier

entries.text: Solaris now runs on Linux (64-bit): download the AppImage (any distro) or the .deb (Ubuntu, Debian, Mint, Pop!_OS). Both update themselves like on Windows.
Games, Java, mods, modpacks, skins, server hosting (including playit.gg and live CPU/RAM stats) all work on Linux.
Finds the Java installed by your distro, and on laptops with two graphics cards can run Minecraft on the fast one.
Starts normally on Ubuntu 24.04 and newer, where many Electron apps fail to open.
Game and server consoles no longer slow the launcher down while big modpacks start: log lines are drawn in batches.
Mod lists open faster: mod names and icons are remembered between sessions instead of re-reading every jar.
Solaris opens a little faster, and Java detection checks all Javas at once.
“Clean up storage” no longer deletes the OptiFine versions you imported or the running playit.gg agent.
A stuck internet connection can no longer freeze “Downloading game files” forever — Solaris retries instead.
Stopping a server while it was still preparing Java now really stops it.
Sending a command to a server at the moment it closed could crash Solaris in the background.
Server backups on Paper and Purpur no longer store the Nether and End twice.
Closing the window while hosting and playing no longer shuts your server down when the game closes.
Moving the data folder is blocked while games or servers run, and into a folder inside itself.
The right native libraries are picked for your computer’s processor.

title: Our own Solaris Client mod

entries.text: The Solaris Client now has its own mod, made by Solaris: press Right Shift in game for the Solaris menu.
Movable HUD: FPS, CPS, keystrokes, coordinates with direction, ping and a clock. Drag them anywhere in “Edit HUD layout”.
Hold C to zoom, and turn on toggle sprint from the Solaris menu. Your settings are saved.
OneConfig, EvergreenHUD, PolySprint and Zoomify are now optional extras (off by default) — the Solaris mod does those jobs.

title: Hosting: every server type, playit.gg, backups and more

entries.text: Create Vanilla, Paper, Purpur, Fabric, Forge and NeoForge servers — pick the version, memory, max players, port and folder. Solaris downloads everything.
Public address with playit.gg for any server type (free account, connected once), or e4mc for Fabric/Forge/NeoForge (no account). Tunnel status and automatic reconnects.
Dashboard with status, players, CPU, RAM, uptime and address. Start, stop, restart, open folder, settings and delete.
Server page: live console (clear, auto-scroll, errors only), players, whitelist and operators, worlds, backups and restore, log files, and a full server.properties editor.
Install mods and plugins from Modrinth, checked against your server’s version and software — or start a server from a modpack.
Skins now really change: each wardrobe skin has a Wear button, and the skin you wear is marked. Clicking a skin only previews it.
Your current skin is read live from your Microsoft account, so a new skin shows right away instead of a minute later.
Deleting an instance removes it for good instead of moving it to the Recycle Bin.

title: Host servers, in-game client menu and skins that show up

entries.text: New Host page: create a Minecraft server on your PC in a few clicks, start it, and share a public address — no port forwarding, no account. Live console, players, kick, settings, whitelist.
Solaris stops your servers properly when you quit, so worlds are saved.
In-game client menu like Lunar: press Right Shift for one menu with your mods, a HUD editor and settings (OneConfig by Polyfrost).
New modules: PolySprint (toggle sprint/sneak) and Chatting (chat tabs and search).
“Wear this skin” now checks with Mojang that your skin really changed, and tells you clearly if it didn’t.
Offline accounts can wear skins too — Solaris adds CustomSkinLoader to modded instances so your skin shows in game.
Installing a mod, pack or shader now turns the button green with “Installed” and a check, so you know it worked.
New icons from Lucide.
Player look-ups fall back to minetools when Mojang is busy.
World hosting picks up the e4mc address even when it is hidden in chat.

title: New look, OptiFine, hosting for friends and cosmetics

entries.text: New Solaris logo and new fonts (Plus Jakarta Sans and Outfit) — including a cleaner Play button.
Faster start: Home shows modpacks, news and player counts from last time instantly, and the 3D skin viewer only loads when you need it.
Optional cosmetics: Capes (see OptiFine, LabyMod and MinecraftCapes capes), 3D Skin Layers, Wavey Capes, Emotecraft and Ears.
Host for friends: with e4mc, Open to LAN puts your world online without port forwarding. Solaris shows the address and an invite link.
New modules like Feather and OneClient: EvergreenHUD (FPS, CPS, keystrokes), Controlling, FastQuit, Chat Heads, World Host, More Culling and more.
AppleSkin’s settings page works again (Cloth Config is added automatically).
Play together: host your world, join a friend by address or invite link, and see when you are hosting.
OptiFine for vanilla instances: download OptiFine from optifine.net, import it, and Solaris installs it. Pick OptiFine when creating an instance or in Change version.
See the release notes of a new version while it downloads, before you restart.

title: Minecraft news, solaris:// links and snowfall

entries.text: Minecraft news: the latest Java Edition news from Mojang right on Home. Click a card to read the full article.
New animated splash screen while Solaris starts.
solaris:// links open Solaris straight to a Modrinth modpack (solaris://modrinth/<name>) or offer to join a server (solaris://server/<address>). Links never install or launch anything without you.
Snowfall: gentle falling snow, on by itself in December. Switch it in Settings → Appearance.
Update files are now named Solaris-Setup-x.y.z.exe, so releases upload to GitHub without renaming.

title: Sign-in screen, self-updates and Discord buttons

entries.text: New sign-in screen: sign in with Microsoft or pick an offline name before you start, with a live 3D preview of your player.
Solaris now updates itself: new versions download in the background with a progress animation, then install with one click.
“What’s new” pops up once after each update.
No more “Update failed” message when there simply isn’t a new version yet.
Rich Presence works out of the box — no application ID to paste. It now uses Silent Client’s discord-rpc, shows a “Get Solaris” button and reconnects by itself when you open Discord later.
Animated capes in the 3D viewer, and a button to preview your own cape file (idea from Silent Client’s skinview3d).

title: CurseForge, friends and a lot more

entries.text: CurseForge: browse and install mods, modpacks, shaders and resource packs (add your free API key in Settings → Integrations).
Modpack updates: update a Modrinth or CurseForge modpack, or switch to any version. Your worlds, settings and own mods are kept.
Source badges show where every mod came from: Modrinth, CurseForge, a modpack, or added by you.
Import CurseForge modpack .zip files and CurseForge app instances.
New Files, Screenshots and Logs tabs: a built-in file explorer and config editor, per-instance screenshots, and crash logs you can upload to mclo.gs.
Reorder or hide instance tabs in Settings → Appearance.
Damaged game files are detected automatically and repaired on the next launch.
Friends: follow players, see their real skins, and see when Solaris spots them on a server.
New mods are scanned for malware automatically, plus Scan now in Settings → Privacy & safety.
Discord shows your player head for Microsoft accounts, with privacy switches for what is shared.
Refresh skin button, streamer mode, and warnings for unusual offline usernames.
Light, dark or match-system mode, a Classic layout, and custom gradients for buttons and the background.
Low-end PC mode and a GPU acceleration switch in Settings → Performance.
Smarter Java: per-version Java choices, a Test button, and Java that is too old is skipped automatically.
If your moved data folder is missing (e.g. an unplugged drive), Solaris asks what to do instead of starting empty.

title: Solaris is here

entries.text: Launch every Minecraft: Java Edition release, snapshot and old version from one launcher.
Multi-instancing: run several instances at the same time, each with its own live console.
Automatic Java: the right official Java runtime is downloaded for every version.
Quick Play: join a server or open a world straight from the launcher.
Auto memory sizing based on your system RAM, with per-instance overrides.
Performance mode and dedicated-GPU preference for laptops.
Fabric, Quilt, Forge, NeoForge and Legacy Fabric — loaders only show up on compatible versions.
Duplicate instances with selective copying of mods, packs, worlds and config.
Share instances as .solpack files and import .mrpack modpacks by drag & drop.
Custom icons, pinned favourites, readable folder names and play-time tracking.
Import from the official launcher, MultiMC and Prism Launcher.
Built-in Modrinth browser for mods, modpacks, resource packs, shaders and datapacks.
Version picker, automatic required dependencies and multi-category filters.
Bulk select, enable, disable and delete with Ctrl/Shift+Click.
Update manager that checks every mod against Modrinth by file hash.
Duplicate-mod detection and a heuristic malware scan.
One-click all-in-one modpack: Sodium, Lithium, FerriteCore, Zoomify and more, kept up to date on every launch.
Toggle modules per instance from the Solaris Client page.
Server browser with live player counts, ping, MOTD, region & tag filters and favourites.
Server statistics: player count history for every server you check.
Skin wardrobe with a 3D preview, staged Apply, and cape switching for Microsoft accounts.
Discord Rich Presence.
Crash assistant explains crashes in plain language with suggested fixes and hex exit codes.
Live console with filtering and one-click log sharing to mclo.gs.
Hosts-file check for blocked Mojang/Microsoft domains.
Themes with live preview, custom accent colours and a custom theme editor.
Editable keybinds, mouse back/forward navigation and instant language switching.
Gallery of screenshots across all instances.
Storage manager: see what uses space, clean up unused files and move the data folder.
